summary: This bill establishes a tax on greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuels, industrial processes, and certain products, using the generated revenue to fund infrastructure projects, energy programs, and provide assistance to displaced energy workers, while also implementing border tax adjustments for imports and exports and creating a National Climate Commission to set emissions reduction goals.

scores.thoughts: Title I establishes the 'Rebuilding Infrastructure and Solutions for the Environment Trust Fund' (RISE Trust Fund) which receives 75% of the revenues from new greenhouse gas taxes. This fund then appropriates significant percentages to various programs, including the Highway Trust Fund, weatherization programs, assistance for displaced energy workers, the Airport and Airway Trust Fund, and several research and development initiatives. Title II also appropriates funds for cancer research. Title VII authorizes additional appropriations for school safety. These provisions clearly indicate a substantial increase in government spending across multiple sectors, funded by new taxes.

Title I of the bill introduces a new subtitle to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, imposing a tax on fossil fuels, industrial process greenhouse gas emissions, and greenhouse gas emissions from certain manufactured products. It also repeals federal motor vehicle and aviation fuel taxes, but the new greenhouse gas taxes are a significant new revenue stream. The bill explicitly details the rates and mechanisms for these new taxes, making taxation a central component.

The bill establishes a National Bipartisan Fiscal Commission tasked with reviewing and recommending a legislative package to stabilize long-term deficits and debt, and requiring the Congressional Budget Office to consider the cost of servicing the debt in its estimations. This indicates a direct focus on prioritizing debt reduction and fiscal responsibility, even while other parts of the bill increase spending and taxation.
